content: 1. Ritonavir's levels or effects can be increased by erythromycin lactobionate through inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Ritonavir can increase the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate can also increase ritonavir levels via the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs, and monitor closely. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Close monitoring is advised. 4. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin stearate also increases ritonavir levels via the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs, and monitor closely. 5. Ritonavir increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome and toxicity. Use caution, monitor closely, and adjust therapy as needed. 6. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases ritonavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Ritonavir increases esomeprazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Ritonavir increases estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies if necessary. 9. Ritonavir increases estradiol vaginal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase estrogen plasma concentrations and toxicities. Monitor closely. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ritonavir increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies. 14. Ritonavir increases ethinyl estradiol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use non-hormonal contraceptives and monitor closely. 15. Ritonavir increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may increase toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ritonavir increases etonogestrel levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ritonavir increases etoposide levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ritonavir increases etravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Etravirine decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated with certain ritonavir preparations. Monitor closely and consider alternative therapies. 19. Ritonavir increases eucalyptus levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Ritonavir increases everolimus levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Ritonavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension, potentially due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia. 22. Ritonavir and ezogabine may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QT interval. Monitor the QT interval closely, especially at higher ezogabine doses. 23. Fedratinib increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Ritonavir also increases fedratinib levels. Co-administration is contraindicated unless dose adjustments are made. Monitor closely for toxicities. 24. Ritonavir increases felbamate levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 25. Ritonavir increases felodipine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Felodipine also increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ritonavir increases fentanyl levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration requires frequent monitoring for respiratory depression and sedation, with dose adjustments as needed. Avoid co-administration if possible. 27. Ritonavir increases fesoterodine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Ritonavir decreases fexinidazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Fexinidazole also increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 29. Ritonavir increases fexofenadine levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Ritonavir increases finasteride levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 31. Ritonavir increases finerenone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Ritonavir increases flecainide levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism and decreasing its clearance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Ritonavir increases flibanserin levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 34. Fluconazole increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ritonavir increases fludrocortisone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely for toxicities. 36. Ritonavir increases flunisolide inhaled levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Ritonavir increases fluoxetine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 38. Ritonavir increases fluphenazine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 39. Ritonavir increases flurazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider lowering benzodiazepine doses, monitor closely, and use alternatives if available. 40. Ritonavir increases fluticasone furoate levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure. Monitor closely for signs of Cushing syndrome. 41. Ritonavir increases fluticasone inhaled levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid exposure. Monitor closely. 42. Ritonavir increases fluticasone intranasal levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of systemic corticosteroid adverse effects, including Cushing syndrome. 43. Ritonavir increases fluvastatin toxicity by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, increasing the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Fluvoxamine increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Food increases ritonavir levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Fosamprenavir increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 47. Fosaprepitant increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 48. Fosphenytoin decreases ritonavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Fostamatinib increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib's active metabolite). Monitor for toxicities and adjust doses as needed. 50. Ritonavir increases futibatinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
